_doc: Focus roster for steward-focus.yml (heartbeat scheduler, cron */10 UTC — a tick every ~10 minutes; drop to */5 to run harder). Each tick fires one improve run per enabled lane that is due AND idle: a lane fires its next batch within ~10 min of the last one finishing (skip-if-busy waits out any active slice), and a batch that died mid-way restarts on the next tick instead of stalling. Lane fields beyond enabled/everyHours (all optional): offset (which hours the cadence lands on — hourUTC % everyHours === offset, so 'align next run to 21:00' is offset = 21 % everyHours), window ([startUTC,endUTC) hour window, wraps midnight), startAt (ISO — lane sleeps until then), until (ISO — lane expires then; 'run every X until Y'), slices (1..10, default 1 — the lane's standing CONCURRENCY TARGET: how many improve runs it keeps going AT ALL TIMES; each is a full separate unit of work with its own PR + smoke gate). steward-focus TOPS THE LANE UP each tick: it counts how many of the N slots are occupied and dispatches only the empty ones, so a run finishing frees one slot and one replacement starts while its siblings carry on. It refills that slot's OWN number (slice=k), which matters twice: the slice index is part of steward-improve's concurrency group, and slice k takes the k-th topmost workable item — stable because a claimed item keeps its place in the list (see improve.md § PARALLEL SLICES; chicago/4d additionally locks with tools/ticket.mjs claim/inflight). This replaced a BATCH GATE, which fired all N and then skipped the lane until every one had finished — so the lane moved at the pace of its slowest run, and a lane set to 10 spent much of its time running one. A freed slot does NOT wait for a cron tick: the finishing run dispatches steward-focus itself, so the lane is back to full strength within about a minute (GitHub throttles scheduled events badly under load, so the cron is only a backstop — it also covers a slot freed by a run that FAILED, which deliberately does not kick). For continuous operation keep everyHours at 1, which makes the lane eligible on every tick; a coarser cadence only tops the lane up on the hours it is due. Raise it to grind an app harder; hard-capped at 10 (10 concurrent agent runs on one app is a lot of tokens and a lot of open PRs for the janitor — step up gradually). Evaluated by .github/steward/schedule.mjs (the canonical logic — `node .github/steward/schedule.mjs next` previews every lane). Edit this file from the GitHub UI, any Claude session, or Manager's Fleet Ops panel — changes take effect on the next tick (~10 min), no workflow edits needed. Different apps run in parallel, and so do a lane's own slices; a lane never exceeds its slices target, and a lowered target is honoured by waiting for the surplus to drain rather than cancelling it. The `jobs` section schedules the platform-level recurring jobs with the SAME lane fields (slices excepted): fleet-improve (suite-wide steward pick), sweep-ux, sweep-tech, janitor — their standalone workflow crons are retired; this roster is the single scheduler. Per-lane `model` (optional) pins the Claude model for that lane's runs (e.g. claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5, claude-haiku-4-5); empty/absent = the fleet default, claude-opus-5 (applied in steward-improve.yml). Editable here or from Manager's Fleet Ops roster.
